edits.english: B GEMARA Rav and Shmuel disagreed concerning the version of the wording of the Mishnah. One teaches [one of them teaches]: “Eideihen,” and one teaches [and one of them teaches]: “Eideihen.” And the Gemara remarks: The one who teaches [whoever teaches] “eideihen” is not mistaken [erring], and the one who teaches [and whoever teaches] “eideihen” is not mistaken [erring], as there is room for both versions.

There are several other instances in the Gemara of a similar dispute regarding the exact wording of the Mishnah. This provides some evidence that the Mishnah was not yet a written text; although it had been edited and arranged, it was still studied orally (see Gittin 60a–b).

edits.hebrew: בנוסף לפירוש הגמרא למונח זה, יש מן המפרשים המציעים כי המקור והמשמעות של המילה "עידיהן" הכתובה בעי"ן קשורה אולי לכתוב "בגד עדים" (ישעיהו סד, ה). כמו כן, ייתכן שיש קשר בין המונח "איד" לבין ה"אידוס" (Ides), אמצע החודש המקודש בלוח השנה הרומי.
